claim_limitation: E1 attribution census for campaign UD-GFX1151-OPTIMIZE2. It ranks where UD-Q4_K_M prefill time goes against plain Q4_K_M at the matched 512-token shape and verifies that both arms' census owners are reached through hipengine.LLM.generate(). No routing policy, kernel, or default changed to produce it, so no post-change rate is claimed and no lever is promoted from this artifact alone.
question: Where does UD-Q4_K_M prefill time go versus plain Q4_K_M on zbook/gfx1151 at 512 tokens, which hypotheses does that adjudicate, and does the shipped surface reach the same owners?

host.cpu: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 w/ Radeon 8060S
host.lane_note: zbook lane, not the desktop gfx1151 lane. Same-GPU-architecture peers are independent lanes (docs/OPTIMIZATION.md section 2).

provenance.env_incident: A first identical census ran 2026-09-23T16:12-16:34+09:00 from /tmp/ud-prefill-census; the host was rebooted 2026-09-24T18:12+09:00 and /tmp (a separate mount) was wiped with it, destroying those traces, rank tables and logs. This artifact records the post-reboot re-run from durable storage. The pre-reboot readout, preserved only in the executing session's transcript, matched this run's tables to within about 1 percent on every ranked share (plain window 1847.8 -> 1687.9 ms, UD 2865.8 -> 2640.3 ms, window ratio 1.551 -> 1.564), so the census is treated as reproduced rather than as a first observation; the pre-reboot files themselves are not recoverable.

protocol.shape: one resident session: warm-up prefill of --prefill-tokens plus 4 eager steps, reset() with weights and scratch retained, 0.5 s GPU idle gap, one measured fresh 512-token bulk prefill
protocol.windowing: every KERNEL_DISPATCH after the last >=0.4 s inter-kernel gap, i.e. the trailing burst after the idle gap (same trailing-burst logic the decode census uses, no marker trace)
protocol.jit_policy: warm build outside the profiler against the pinned HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE, then the profiled run sets require_cached_build=1 so the profiled process spawns no hipcc/clang (docs/OPTIMIZATION.md section 7)
protocol.rocprofv3: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace --output-format csv -d OUT -o NAME -- python3 scripts/gguf_decode_graph_rocprof_driver.py MODEL prefill --max-sequence-length 8192
protocol.profiled_overhead: profiled run is 2.1 percent (plain) and 1.2 percent (UD) below the unprofiled repro of the same driver
protocol.harness_agreement: the unprofiled repro measures 306.144 tok/s plain and 195.253 UD (ratio 0.6378); the committed 2026-09-23 paired sweep medians at 512/128 are 296.433 and 187.780 (ratio 0.6335). Driver absolutes run 3-4 percent above the sweep (isolated single prefill on an idle cool host versus the sweep's interleaved window); the ratio, which is what attribution uses, reproduces within 0.7 percent.

hypothesis_verdicts.H1: REFUTED as stated. The prefill gap is not raw-layout tensors running GEMV-shaped owners: both arms run WMMA prefill families throughout, and misc GEMV is 0.2 percent of the UD window (2.2 percent of plain). The census instead ranks the dense-IQ one-wave W4A16 owner at 48.18 percent of the UD window (1272.1 ms, 135 launches across 4 templates, IQ4_XS alone 1020.1 ms at 8719 us/launch) and the Q5_T16 WMMA family at 24.81 percent (655.0 ms) as the two pots that explain the +952.4 ms window delta.
hypothesis_verdicts.H12_E9: CONFIRMED as the largest single prefill lever and now sized: the 48.18 percent sitting in gguf_iq_prefill_wmma is exactly the one-wave owner that E9's coop/coop64 overrides target. Mechanism arithmetic only (gfx1100 record, not a gfx1151 rate): a 1.5x leaf improvement on that family moves the window ratio 0.6393 -> about 0.76, a 2x -> about 0.84; parity still requires the Q5_T16 pot as well.
hypothesis_verdicts.H3_H5_prefill_layout: LIVE FACT FOR E3a: the shipped LLM.generate() path resolves T16 layout keys (gguf_q4_k_t16_v1, gguf_q5_k_t16_v1, gguf_q6_k_t16_qmicro_planar_v1, gguf_q8_0_t16_v1) for the UD file while the committed route audit records repack=OFF with those families on raw-gguf-kernel. Either the audit describes a different surface than materialization, or the admission chain changed behavior; E3a must locate the divergence before any layout change is written. E1 does not resolve which side is stale.
hypothesis_verdicts.H7: RANKED LOW for prefill: Q8_0 T16 prefill wmma + rowtile gemv total 71.5 ms (2.7 percent) and Q6 families total 66.8 ms (2.5 percent) on UD; they are behind the IQ and Q5 pots in this census.
hypothesis_verdicts.H8: NO THRESHOLD ARTIFACT OBSERVED at the census shape: the unprofiled ladder moves monotonically for both arms (plain 297.3/306.1/307.3/296.6/291.8 and UD 191.2/195.3/191.0/179.3/173.9 tok/s at 256/512/768/2048/4096), with the UD/plain ratio drifting smoothly 0.643 -> 0.596 as rows grow. The widening gap at long prompts is a real row-scaling effect, not a cusp at 512; owner-band sweeps below/above unrelated values remain E3/E9 work.

limitations: performance_claim false: no paired A/B, no quality gate, no lever changed.
rocprofv3 --kernel-trace exposes timing and launch geometry only; no memory-throughput or occupancy counters were collected, so bytes/s per family (campaign section 1.1) is not measured here.

The prefill window is weight-read-tensor with compute-bound leaves: summed dense-IQ family time reads roughly 5.5 GB of weights in 1272 ms (about 4 GB/s), i.e. far below the 186 GB/s streaming roof, consistent with WMMA compute/occupancy limits rather than bandwidth - an inference from byte counts and window time, not a hardware counter measurement.
One shape (512 tokens) is census-profiled; 256/768/2048/4096 are unprofiled wall-clock only.

Family deltas compare two different weight compositions (campaign section 1.1): plain streams Q4_K-heavy weights, UD Q5_K/IQ4_XS-heavy weights, so per-family deltas are attribution, not like-for-like leaf benchmarks.
